answer: Each identity files one self-audit on the wharf ledger listing failed deliveries, seals it with its pigment seal, and locks a 70-credit bond plus a 20-credit fee. Auditors check it against the willow board. A willow-board failure missing from the filing counts as concealment and burns the bond and 40 credits. The k-th fake still pays 90 for its distinct record: one filing per identity, and a copy voids both. 1,000 fakes risk 90,000 credits; one honest identity pays 90 once and keeps its bond. A rented-audit ring fails: rented filings carry the renter's pigment seal, visible at the wharf.
